steps.message: The "tidy up" commit changed 90 to 95; the comment and tests say 10% off.

arguments.command:
sed -i 's|base \* 95|base * 90|' bin/price
mkdir -p changes && printf 'ticket: CART-58\n\nFix member price: restore 10%% discount (was accidentally changed to 5%% in "price: tidy up").\n' > changes/CART-58.md
git add -A && git commit -qm "[CART-58] fix member price discount back to 10%

steps.message:
The price test now passes. The "price: tidy up" commit had changed the member discount from `* 90 / 100` to `* 95 / 100`, which is 5% off instead of the 10% the comment and tests expect. I changed it back in `bin/price`.

- **Change note:** `changes/CART-58.md` is added.
- **Commit:** `[CART-58] fix member price discount back to 10%`.
- **Verification:** `bash scripts/verify.sh` ran after the last edit and passed.
- **Issue:** I added the `needs-check` label to #31. I haven't merged or closed anything.
